claim_tested: WOPR domain makes base-specific DNA contacts that define a predictable consensus
key_finding: Recomputed here: 104 contacts <4.0 A, 76 to sugar/phosphate, 28 to bases. Base-reading residues Arg65, Ser75, Arg76, Leu82, Tyr84. Only Ser75 OG-cytosine N4 (2.91 A) is a discriminating H-bond; Arg65's 17 contacts are minor-groove O2/N3 (A/T tract, not base order); Tyr84/Leu82 are carbon shape contacts. Read span bp5-9 = GTTTA.
context: C. albicans Wor1 WOPRa+WOPRb fusion with 13 bp and 17 bp duplexes from the WOR1 promoter
confidence: High for contact geometry (direct from deposited coordinates). Limitation: one DNA sequence only, so positions that could tolerate variation are untested.

evidence_type: direct assay (in vitro DNA binding, mutational analysis)
claim_tested: Wor1 WOPR box is a sequence-specific DNA-binding domain with a defined site
key_finding: WOPR box binds DNA as a monomer; a 14 bp site was identified; neither WOPRa nor WOPRb alone binds specifically, both are required.
confidence: High for the family-level MF assignment. Limitation: the site was defined for Wor1, not for Rof1 or Mit1; no PWM was deposited in a public motif database.

claim_tested: The WOPR base-reading surface is identical in Wor1, Mit1 and Rof1
key_finding: All 5 base-contacting residues identical: Wor1 R65/S75/R76/L82/Y84 = Rof1 R63/S73/R74/L80/Y82 = Mit1 R62/S72/R73/L79/Y81. 12 of 14 total contact positions identical; the 2 exceptions (T210->S, I232->I/V) are backbone contacts. Rof1 retains a WOPRb block at ~116-202 (35.6% identity to Wor1 185-300) despite a short Pfam PF09729 footprint.
context: Sequence/structure inference, S. cerevisiae and C. albicans
confidence: Medium-high. Limitation: inference from alignment, not from a Rof1 structure or a Rof1 binding assay.

evidence_type: computational (genome-wide motif scan, R64-1-1, Markov-3 background)
claim_tested: The structure-derived consensus can nominate Rof1 direct targets
key_finding: GTTTA: 30,719 genomic occurrences vs 29,519 expected (1.04x), in 84.7% of 700 bp promoters. Full 13 bp crystal duplex: 0 occurrences (2.0 expected). FLO11 rank 1990/6572 (44th pct), FLO10 and TEC1 rank 865 (22nd pct); permutation p=0.233. The 9 bp AAGTTTAAC marks 61 functionally incoherent promoters and excludes all three genes.
context: S. cerevisiae S288C genome, 6,572 protein-coding promoters
confidence: High. Limitation: consensus-string scanning, not PWM scanning; no experimental PWM exists to test.

claim_tested: The negative result reflects motif information content, not a broken pipeline
key_finding: Rap1 13 bp 2.48x enriched (2.1% of promoters); Mcm1 16 bp 2.80x (0.5%); Gcn4 TGACTCA 7 bp 1.00x (5.6%); Ste12 TGAAACA 7 bp 0.93x (16.5%). Short sites are at chance even for bona fide specific TFs.
context: S. cerevisiae genome, same scan parameters
confidence: High. Limitation: consensus strings underestimate what full PWMs plus chromatin context can achieve.

evidence_type: direct assay (transposon Calling Cards, genome-wide TF binding)
claim_tested: Direct targets of filamentation regulators are definable in vivo
key_finding: 28 TFs mapped in nitrogen-starved yeast; DNA-binding preferences for central filamentation regulators (Flo8, Mss11, Mfg1) had been unknown and were derived from the binding data, not predicted from structure.
context: S. cerevisiae, nitrogen starvation, in vivo
confidence: High as a methodological precedent. Limitation: whether ROF1 or MIT1 were among the 28 TFs was not verified here.

claim_tested: A usable experimental WOPR position weight matrix is publicly available
key_finding: 417 fungal matrices; none for Wor1, Mit1, Rof1 or YHR177W. CIS-BP could not be queried from this environment (HTTP 404), so its contents were not established.
confidence: High for JASPAR, not established for CIS-BP.
